title: Nested layouts
summary: Persistent client-side layouts with independently owned data.

sections.title: Choose the nested entry
sections.body: Import nested rendering and data hooks from the same nested adapter. This optional entry reuses the data router; flat imports do not retain its layout implementation. This release supports client-only route trees, not renderApplication/mountApplication nested SSR.

sections.title: File layouts
sections.body: applicationPlugins({ ssr: false }) recognizes actual parent route modules. The virtual route module exports createRouter and Routes for the detected tree. Names such as _authorized.settings and _authorized.settings.profile establish ownership; filenames supply IDs and paths. Leading underscores are pathless and _index selects an index child. Optional layout code is absent when no parent modules exist.
sections.code:
import routes, { createRouter, Routes } from "virtual:smolter/routes";
const router = createRouter(routes, { browser: true });

sections.title: Data and refresh ownership
sections.body: Each layout reads its own useLoaderData value. useRouteLoaderData reads an ancestor by ID. Target one or several layout IDs to refresh only those owners; untargeted ancestors and descendants keep their data. shouldRevalidate remains authoritative, including manual refresh. Initial loading cannot be vetoed.
sections.code:
await router.revalidate({ route: "account" });
await router.revalidate({ route: ["root", "account"] });

sections.title: Forms and boundaries
sections.body: Forms and fetchers default to their owning route. Index submissions include ?index to distinguish them from their parent. Explicit actions and fetcher URLs respect basename. The nearest layout ErrorBoundary handles loader, action and render failures; navigating to a valid route clears its rendering error. Shared layout state remains mounted across children.

sections.title: Loading and transitions
sections.body: Layouts without loaders stay mounted while a child loader is pending. The loading child owns its HydrateFallback. Export viewTransition(commit, previous, next) from a page to own its presentation. The destination page wins; otherwise its nearest layout export is used. Without an export, Smolter commits immediately. Both adapters and flat mounted applications support the same callback. Smolter does not start animations or select CSS, duration or reduced-motion policy. Call commit once; stale and repeated calls are ignored. The callback return value is not awaited, so consumers own completing the commit and handling animation promises/errors. Initial loading, errors and same-URL updates can also commit: choose which updates to animate in your callback.

sections.title: Shared-image transitions
sections.body: Your callback can pass commit to document.startViewTransition. Give the old and new image the same unique view-transition-name in consumer CSS. The browser captures the old image before the commit and the new image afterward, and animates between them. Keep image dimensions stable and prepare/decode the destination image before committing when necessary. A matching name must identify only one rendered element per state. Browser support, reduced motion, skipped/rejected transitions and animation styling remain consumer responsibilities. Smolter does not promise flash-free remote image loading or add a second animation system.
sections.code:
/* Apply this class to the corresponding image on both pages. */
.shared-artwork { view-transition-name: artwork; }

sections.title: Unused capabilities
sections.body: Smolter’s Vite plugin keeps the nested engine out of flat file-route applications. It also removes transition dispatch when no analyzed route exports viewTransition and application construction uses the generated virtual routes. Manual factories, opaque references, namespace imports and computed writes retain transition support conservatively. Without the plugin, transition support remains available. Neither optimization disables route retention, recovery protection or scroll restoration. Nested routing remains client-only.
